pride_data.title: BioID-screening reveals the Alk “proximitome” of the Drosophila brain
pride_data.projectDescription: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (Alk) is an evolutionary conserved receptor tyrosine kinase of the insulin receptor family. In addition to its well-studied role in cancer, numerous studies on invertebrate and vertebrate models reveal that Alk-signaling is associated with a variety of complex traits such as: regulation of growth and metabolism, hibernation, regulation of neurotransmitters, synaptic coupling, axon targeting, decision making, memory formation and learning, alcohol use disorder, as well as steroid hormone metabolism. To shed light on ALK-driven signaling processes, we used BioID-based in vivo proximity labeling to reveal the molecules that interact with Alk in the Drosophila CNS. Therefore, we generated first and next generation BioID fusion proteins in the endogenous Alk locus by CRISPR/Cas9 induced homology-directed repair (HDR) resulting in viable and fertile flies. Our results show (i) that the next generation of BioID proteins (TurboID and miniTurbo) outperform the first generation BirA* fusion in terms of labeling efficiency, and (ii) allow identification of proximitomes without overexpression which are likely to be more physiologically relevant. LC-MS/MS-based BioID screening of the larval brain revealed an extensive neuronal Alk-proximitome identifying numerous novel potential components of Alk signaling complexes. Validation of Alk-proximitome candidates further revealed co-expression with Alk in the CNS.
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: The streptavidin beads with attached proteins were washed twice with 1 ml 50 mM triethylammonium bicarbonate (TEAB) and digested with 0.5 µg LysC Mass Spec grade (Promega) in 100 µl 50 mM TEAB at 37 °C for 3h with flipping the tubes every 30 min. The samples were reduced in 5 mM tris(2-carboxyethyl)phosphine (TCEP) for 30 min at room temperature and alkylated in 10 mM methyl methanethiosulfonate (MMTS) for 30 min at room temperature. A second digestion was performed with 0.3 µg Pierce MS grade Trypsin (Thermo Fisher Scientific) at 37°C overnight. Next morning the digested samples were removed from beads with a magnetic stand and the beads were washed twice with 50 µl 50 mM TEAB that were pooled with the supernatants. Digested peptides were labelled using Tandem Mass Tag reagents (TMTpro, Thermo Fisher Scientific) according to the manufacturer´s instructions. The combined set was pre-fractionated into 5 and 10 fractions using Pierce High pH Reversed-Phase Peptide Fractionation Kit (Thermo Scientific) according to the manufacturer’s protocol. The fractions were dried in a vacuum centrifuge and reconstituted in 3% acetonitrile, 0.1% formic acid for analysis. The fractions were analyzed on an Orbitrap Fusion™ Lumos™ Tribrid™ mass spectrometer interfaced with an Easy-nLC1200 liquid chromatography system (both Thermo Fisher Scientific). Peptides were trapped on an Acclaim Pepmap 100 C18 trap column (100 μm x 2 cm, particle size 5 μm, Thermo Fischer Scientific) and separated on an in-house packed analytical column i.d. 75 μm, particle size 3 μm, Reprosil-Pur C18, Dr. Maisch, length 35 cm using a linear gradient from 5% to 33% B over 77 min followed by an increase to 100% B for 3 min, and 100% B for 10 min at a flow of 300 nL/min. Solvent A was 0.2% formic acid and solvent B was 80% acetonitrile, 0.2% formic acid. Precursor ion mass spectra were acquired at 120 000 resolution and MS/MS analysis was performed in a data-dependent multinotch mode where CID spectra of the most intense precursor ions were recorded in the ion trap with collision energy setting of 30 for 3 s (‘top speed’ setting). Precursors were isolated in the quadrupole with a 0.7 m/z isolation window, charge states 2 to 7 were selected for fragmentation, dynamic exclusion was set to 45 s and 10 ppm. MS3 spectra for reporter ion quantitation were recorded at 50 000 resolution with HCD fragmentation at collision energy of and 55 using the synchronous precursor selection.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: All data files were merged for identification and relative quantification using Proteome 2.4 (Thermo Fisher Scientific). The data matching was against Drosophila melanogaster from Uniprot (Swissprot+TrEMBL) using Mascot version 2.5.1 (Matrix Science) as a search engine. The precursor mass tolerance was set to 5 ppm and fragment mass tolerance to 0.6 Da. Tryptic peptides were accepted with one missed cleavage, variable modifications of methionine oxidation and fixed cysteine alkylation, TMTpro-label modifications of N-terminal and lysine were selected. Percolator was used for the validation of identified proteins (confidence threshold medium (<5%) and high (<1%)). TMT reporter ions were identified in the MS3 HCD spectra with 3 mmu mass tolerance. Only unique peptides for a given protein were considered for quantification of the proteins.
